source.extractionTool: pdftotext (poppler) -enc UTF-8 raw and -layout modes; pdfplumber for sub/superscript and glyph checks
source.usage: Official CISCE board examination paper from the CISCE Archive Library (cisce.org/archive-library); question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.
source.notes: No official marking scheme is published with this paper; questions carry no official answer. ICSE 2023 board examination paper, Chemistry (Science Paper – 2), from the official CISCE Archive Library ZIP bundle ICSE-2023-QPs.zip; every page footer prints 'T23 522' (used as paperCode); the year 2023 comes from the bundle/file name and the 'T23' prefix. Maximum Marks 80, Time allowed Two hours. Section A (Questions 1–2, 40 marks) is compulsory; Section B (Questions 3–8, 10 marks each) says 'Attempt any four questions', so the printed marks in this pack add up to 100 (40 + 6 × 10), which is expected. Question 1 (i)–(xv) are 1-mark MCQs (the [15] is the Question 1 total). Where a printed mark covers several lettered sub-parts (e.g. [2] for (a)–(b)), each sub-part is its own entry with the mark split evenly (marksSource SECTION_INSTRUCTIONS) and the shared instruction repeated in its text. Chemical formula subscripts and ionic charges are printed as smaller lowered/raised glyphs and were rebuilt as Unicode (H₂SO₄, Zn²⁺, e⁻) after checking glyph size and baseline with pdfplumber; reaction arrows are an unmapped Wingdings glyph (U+F0E0) and are rendered as →. The paper prints '200⁰C' with a superscript zero, kept as printed. Figures not reproduced: the alumina-to-aluminium electrolysis sketch (page 5, Q2(ii)) and the two structural formulae for IUPAC naming (page 6, Q2(v)(b)).
